text:
Arrange the following Cobalt complexes in the order of increasing Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) value.

Complexes : $[CoF_{6}]^{3-}_{A},[Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}_{B},[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}_{C}and[Co(en)_{3}]^{3+}_{D}$

Choose the correct option :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(i) CFSE $\propto$ charge or oxidation no. of central metal ion.

(ii) CFSE $\propto$ strength of ligand

$en > NH_{3} > H_{2}O > F^{-}$

(iii) The oxidation state of the metal has the larger effect: Co(III) complexes have a much larger crystal field splitting than Co(II) complexes. So the only Co(II) complex, B, comes lowest even though $H_{2}O$ is a stronger field ligand than $F^{-}$; the three Co(III) complexes then follow ligand strength $(F^{-} < NH_{3} < en)$.

$\therefore$ order of CFSE

$[Co(en)_{3}]^{+3}^{III}>[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{+3}^{III}>[CoF_{6}]^{-3}^{III}>[Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{+2}^{II}$

i.e. increasing order of CFSE : B < A < C < D
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift

text: The number of stereoisomers possible for 1, 2-dimethyl cyclopropane is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane, C1 and C2 are stereocentres: each carries $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and two different ring paths.

In the cis isomer both methyl groups lie on the same face of the ring; a plane of symmetry passes through C3 and the midpoint of the C1–C2 bond, so it is an achiral meso compound: 1 stereoisomer.

In the trans isomer the methyl groups lie on opposite faces; it has no plane or centre of symmetry (only a $C_{2}$ axis, which does not make a molecule achiral), so it exists as a pair of enantiomers: 2 stereoisomers.


[IMG]

Total number of stereoisomers $=1+2=3$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift

text:
In the sulphur estimation, 0.471 g of an organic compound gave 1.44 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is $____________$%. (Nearest integer)

solution.body:

$\because$ 233 BaSO$_{4}$ contain $\to$ 32 g sulphur

% of S = $\frac{32\times 1.44}{233\times 0.471}\times 100=41.98%\approx 42%$

text:
For water $\Delta_{vap}$ H = 41 kJ mol$^{-1}$ at 373 K and 1 bar pressure. Assuming that water vapour is an ideal gas that occupies a much larger volume than liquid water, the internal energy change during evaporation of water is $___________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}$

[Use : R = 8.3 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$H_{2}O(l)$ $\to$ $H_{2}O(g)$ : $\Delta$H = 41 $\frac{kJ}{mol}$

$\Rightarrow$ From the relation : $\Delta$H = $\Delta$U + $\Delta n_{g}RT$

$\Rightarrow$ 41$\frac{kJ}{mol}$ = $\Delta$U + (1) $\times$ $\frac{8.3}{1000}$ $\times$ 373

$\Delta$ DU = 41 $-$ 3.0959 = 38 kJ/mol

text:
A metal surface is exposed to 500 nm radiation. The threshold frequency of the metal for photoelectric current is 4.3 $\times$ $10^{14} Hz$. The velocity of ejected electron is $____________$ $\times$ $10^{5} ms^{-1} ($Nearest integer)

[Use : h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js, m_{e} = 9.0$ $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$υ$ : speed of electron having max. K.E.

 $\Rightarrow$ from Einstein equation : E = $𝜙$ $+ K.E._{\max }$

$\Rightarrow \frac{hc}{λ}=hυ_{0}+\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{6.63\times 10^{-34}\times 3\times 10^{8}}{500\times 10^{-9}}=6.63\times 10^{-34}\times 4.3\times 10^{14}+\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{6.63\times 30\times 10^{-20}}{5}=6.63\times 4.3\times 10^{-20}+\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 11.271\times 10^{-20}J=\frac{1}{2}\times 9\times 10^{-31}\times υ^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $υ$ = 5 $\times$ $10^{5} m/\sec $.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift

text: The overall stability constant of the complex ion [$Cu(NH_{3})_{4}$]$^{2+}$ is 2.1 $\times$ $10^{13}$. The overall dissociations constant is y $\times$ $10^{-14}$. Then y is $__________. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The overall stability (formation) constant refers to

$\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}β_{4}=2.1\times 10^{13}$

The overall dissociation is the reverse reaction, so its constant is the reciprocal of $β_{4}$:

$K_{d}=\dfrac{1}{β_{4}}=\dfrac{1}{2.1\times 10^{13}}=4.76\times 10^{-14}$

So $y=4.76\approx 5$.

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift

text:
83 g of ethylene glycol dissolved in 625 g of water. The freezing point of the solution is $____________ K. ($Nearest integer)

[Use : Molal Freezing point depression constant of water = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$

Freezing Point of water = 273 K

Atomic masses : C : 12.0 u, O : 16.0 u, H : 1.0 u]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$k_{f} = 1.86 K kg/$mol

T${}_{f}^{o}$ = 273 K

solvent : $H_{2}O(625 g)$

Solute : 83 g of ethylene glycol

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta T_{f} = k_{f}$ $\times$ m

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (T_{f}^{o}-T_{f}^{1}\right )=1.86\times \frac{83/62}{625/1000}$

$\Rightarrow 273-T_{f}^{1}=\frac{1.86\times 83\times 1000}{62\times 625}=\frac{154380}{38750}$

$\Rightarrow 273-T_{f}^{1}=4$

$\Rightarrow T_{f}^{1}=269$ K
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift

text:
The reaction rate for the reaction

[PtCl$_{4}$]$^{2-} + H_{2}O$ $⇌$ [$Pt(H_{2}O)Cl_{3}$]$^{-} + Cl^{-}$

was measured as a function of concentrations of different species. It was observed that $\frac{-d\left [[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}\right ]}{dt}=4.8\times 10^{-5}\left [[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}\right ]-2.4\times 10^{-3}\left [[Pt(H_{2}O)Cl_{3}]^{-}\right ][Cl^{-}]$.

where square brackets are used to denote molar concentrations. The equilibrium constant $K_{c} = ____________ . ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rate equation provided in your question describes the rates of the forward and reverse reactions for this chemical system. The equilibrium constant, $K_{c}$, is the ratio of the forward rate constant ($k_{f}$) to the reverse rate constant ($k_{r}$). At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction, so the rate equation simplifies to:

$k_{f}[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}=k_{r}[\text{Pt(H}_{2}\text{O)Cl}_{3}]^{-}[\text{Cl}^{-}]$

Given the rate equation:

$-\frac{d[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}}{dt}=4.8\times 10^{-5}[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}-2.4\times 10^{-3}[\text{Pt(H}_{2}\text{O)Cl}_{3}]^{-}[\text{Cl}^{-}]$

At equilibrium, $-\frac{d[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}}{dt}=0$, so:

$0=4.8\times 10^{-5}[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}-2.4\times 10^{-3}[\text{Pt(H}_{2}\text{O)Cl}_{3}]^{-}[\text{Cl}^{-}]$

Rearranging terms, we find:

$4.8\times 10^{-5}[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}=2.4\times 10^{-3}[\text{Pt(H}_{2}\text{O)Cl}_{3}]^{-}[\text{Cl}^{-}]$

Now, the equilibrium constant $K_{c}$ is defined as the ratio of the concentrations of the products to the reactants, each raised to the power of their stoichiometric coefficients. For the reaction in question, we have:

$K_{c}=\frac{[\text{Pt(H}_{2}\text{O)Cl}_{3}]^{-}[\text{Cl}^{-}]}{[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}}$

Dividing both sides of our rate equation by $[\text{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-}$, we find that:

$K_{c}=\frac{4.8\times 10^{-5}}{2.4\times 10^{-3}}=\frac{1}{50}$ = 0.02

So, the equilibrium constant $K_{c}$ for this reaction is approximately 0, when rounded to the nearest integer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift
